comment: Assigning the architecture to ‘an individual or small team’ with a single authority risks a heroic-architect model, concentration of power, bottlenecks to timelines, and turnover leading to loss of continuity. DPI-H decisions span public health, clinical care, law, privacy, enterprise architecture, implementation, gender/equity and subnational operations; no single professional can legitimately represent all of these.

public.text: Assigning the architecture to ‘an individual or small team’ with a single authority risks a heroic-architect model, concentration of power, bottlenecks to timelines, and turnover leading to loss of continuity. DPI-H decisions span public health, clinical care, law, privacy, enterprise architecture, implementation, gender/equity and subnational operations; no single professional can legitimately represent all of these.
public.suggestedRevision: Specify a multidisciplinary, institutionally anchored architecture function with shared decision rights, documented accountability, subnational and user representation, conflict-of-interest safeguards, succession and knowledge management. A named lead may coordinate, lead with strategic direction, and even have "final word" on decisions if necessary, but should not substitute for collective governance and independent review.
